title: Contraception (India)
specialty: Obstetrics and Gynaecology / Primary Care / Family Planning

evidenceAudit.scope: Contraceptive counselling and provision under the Indian national family planning programme: injectable medroxyprogesterone acetate (Antara), combined oral contraceptive pills (Mala-N), centchroman (Chhaya), copper intrauterine devices including postpartum IUCD, emergency contraception and condoms, with eligibility, timing after childbirth and abortion, side effects and follow-up, using MoHFW reference manuals, FOGSI, WHO and MSF sources.
findings: DMPA 150 mg IM every 3 months (13 weeks), 2 weeks early to 4 weeks late, start 6 weeks postpartum if breastfeeding, immediately after abortion, MEC category 4 conditions, side effects, fertility return 7–10 months, no routine bone density monitoring checked against the MoHFW Injectable Contraceptive (MPA) manual (2016).

Cu IUCD 380A (10 years) and Cu IUCD 375 (5 years), post-placental (within 10 minutes), within 48 hours or intra-caesarean PPIUCD, interval and post-abortion timing, follow-up at 6 weeks or first period, PAINS warning signs and use within 5 days as emergency contraception checked against the MoHFW IUCD manual (2018).
Centchroman twice weekly for 3 months then weekly, safe in breastfeeding, contraindications checked against FOGSI Pankh.
Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg or ulipristal 30 mg up to 120 hours and copper IUD within 5 days checked against WHO (2021).
Ethinylestradiol 30 µg / levonorgestrel 150 µg, missed-pill rules, contraindications, enzyme inducers and breastfeeding advice checked against MSF Essential drugs (2021).
unverifiedSections: The MoHFW oral contraceptive pill manual could not be opened; Mala-N use rules are from the MSF monograph for the same formulation.
Sterilisation (tubectomy and vasectomy) is described only briefly and is not sourced.
The FOGSI centchroman brochure gives no missed-pill rule.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: India's family planning programme offers a basket of free methods: condoms, combined pills (Mala-N), the weekly non-hormonal pill centchroman (Chhaya), the three-monthly injectable Antara (DMPA), copper IUCDs including immediate postpartum and post-abortion insertion, emergency contraceptive pills, and sterilisation. Good care starts with counselling about the woman's needs and medical eligibility, excludes pregnancy, and uses every contact — especially delivery and abortion — to offer a method. Most women can use most methods; key restrictions are oestrogen-containing pills in the first 6 weeks postpartum with breastfeeding, high blood pressure, migraine with aura, smoking over 35 and history of thrombosis.
keyMechanisms: DMPA suppresses ovulation and thickens cervical mucus.
Centchroman is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator that prevents implantation.
Copper ions are toxic to sperm and prevent fertilisation; also work as emergency contraception.

symptoms: Unprotected sex in the last 5 days (emergency contraception)
Side effects: irregular bleeding, amenorrhoea, headache
redFlags: Blood pressure 160/100 mmHg or higher: avoid DMPA and combined pills (MoHFW MEC 4)
Migraine with aura: stop hormonal methods (MoHFW)
IUCD: pain, fever, abnormal discharge, missing strings (PAINS) (MoHFW)
Missed period on any method: pregnancy test
precipitants: Enzyme-inducing drugs (rifampicin, carbamazepine) reducing pill efficacy (MSF)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Persistent or postcoital bleeding needs examination.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Every 3 months; up to 2 weeks early or 4 weeks late without backup.
Within 10 minutes of placenta, within 48 hours of vaginal birth, or at caesarean.
Pills up to 120 hours; copper IUD within 5 days.
Contraindicated before 6 weeks; not recommended 6 weeks to 6 months.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: When pregnancy cannot be reasonably excluded (MoHFW).

clinicalManagement.title: Counsel
actions: Discuss all methods, side effects and return to fertility (MoHFW).

clinicalManagement.title: Provide the method
actions: Offer PPIUCD or post-abortion IUCD at the time of delivery or abortion (MoHFW).
DMPA from 6 weeks postpartum if breastfeeding (MoHFW).
Combined pill not before 6 weeks postpartum with breastfeeding (MSF).

clinicalManagement.title: Emergency contraception
actions: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg or ulipristal 30 mg; copper IUD within 5 days is most effective (WHO).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: IUCD at 6 weeks or first period (MoHFW).
DMPA every 3 months; manage bleeding with NSAIDs or tranexamic acid (MoHFW).

medicationPlan.note: DMPA from the MoHFW MPA manual; IUCD from the MoHFW IUCD manual; centchroman from FOGSI; emergency contraception from WHO; combined pill rules from MSF. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Contraception in the Indian public health system.
learningObjectives: Counsel on the national method basket.
Apply eligibility rules and timing after birth or abortion.
keyPoints: PPIUCD within 10 minutes or 48 hours of birth.
Chhaya twice weekly for 3 months, then weekly.
Emergency pill up to 120 hours; copper IUD within 5 days.
pitfalls: Missing the delivery opportunity for PPIUCD.
Refusing DMPA for late returns without a pregnancy check.
